title: De Miraculis Sancti Martini Episcopi
author: Gregory of Tours

passages.original: Quod videntes multi, cum nullus eum penitus excitare praesumeret, transactis fere duarum aut trium horarum spatiis, excitaverunt eum, 1007 dicentes: Jam hora praeterit. Jubcat domnus lectori lectionem legere; exspectat enim populus valde jam lassus. Respondens autem beatus Ambrosius : Nolite, inquit, turbari. Multum enim mihi valet sic obdormisse, cui tale miraculum Dominus ostendere dignatus est. Nam noveritis fratrem meum Martinum sacerdotem egressum fuisse de corpore, me autem ejus funeri obsequium præbuisse, peractoque ex more servitio, capitellum tantum, vobis excitantibus, non explevi.
passages.english: Many who saw this did not dare to wake him at all, but when almost two or three hours had passed, they woke him, saying: "The hour is already passing. Let the lord bishop order the reader to read the lesson, for the people are waiting and are already very weary." But blessed Ambrose answered: "Do not be troubled," he said. "It has been of great benefit to me to have fallen asleep like this, since the Lord has deigned to show me such a miracle. For you should know that my brother Martin, the bishop, has gone forth from the body, and that I rendered service at his funeral; and when the service had been performed according to custom, I did not complete only the closing chapter, because you woke me."
passages.notes: "1007" is a page or column number from the printed edition and has been omitted. "Jubcat" is a scanning error for "Jubeat". "Sacerdotem" is rendered "bishop", as often in this period. "Capitellum" (literally "little chapter") probably means the short closing reading or prayer of the office; the exact sense is uncertain.
